messages.message: The detector's intrinsic efficiency at this distance: the chance a gamma striking the detector face is recorded in the full-energy peak. It is the efficiency used divided by the geometric efficiency, so the two columns multiply to it; for a detector with a characterized response this differs from its far-field curve close to the detector, where gammas interact some way inside the crystal. The uncertainty shown is the detector response's own stated efficiency uncertainty.
The nominal flat-disk solid-angle fraction the detector face takes up at the given distance.
The CPS of the background peaks subtracted from this peak, scaled to the foreground (by the background's display scale factor, or else the ratio of live times).

Gammas per second crossing the face of the detector crystal - a disk of the detector's diameter, at the distance plus the detector setback (or, for a detector with a geometry-modeled response, its modeled crystal).
Gammas per cm² per second at the detector face - that is, at the distance entered. This is what reaches the detector, so it is never corrected for air.

Gammas per second the source gives off in all directions, after any shielding. When "Correct for air attenuation" is checked, this includes the gammas the air absorbed or scattered on the way to the detector, so is then larger than Flux (ɣ/cm²/s) × 4πd².

The source's gamma emission rate (per unit area, or mass, for those types of detector response), from the fixed-geometry efficiency. That efficiency usually already accounts for attenuation within the modeled geometry, so this is the rate the source itself emits, not what makes it out of any shielding.

When checked, the ɣ/4π/s column is corrected for the gammas absorbed or scattered by the air between the source and the detector face, so it is what the source gives off. The flux columns are what reaches the detector, so are not changed - meaning that with this checked, ɣ/4π/s is larger than Flux (ɣ/cm²/s) × 4πd². Not used for fixed-geometry detector responses.

When checked, the area of any background-spectrum peak within one sigma of a foreground peak is subtracted from it, after scaling the background to the foreground (by the background's display scale factor, or else the ratio of live times).
Fixed-geometry detector response: the distance is not used, and ɣ/s{1} is the source's emission rate.
Background peaks scaled by {1}, not by live-time normalization ({2}).
Background peaks scaled by {1}; the background has no live time.
No background peaks are within one sigma of the foreground peaks, so nothing was subtracted.
{1} non-Gaussian background peak(s) could not be used.
The peaks at {1} keV are outside the detector response's {2} keV energy range; their efficiency is extrapolated.
Outside the detector response's {1} keV energy range; the efficiency is extrapolated.

Distance from the center of the source to the face of the detector. The detector crystal sits a little behind the face (the detector response's setback, or for a detector with a geometry-modeled response, its modeled endcap); that is added to this distance when computing the efficiency, while the Flux (ɣ/cm²/s) column is given at this distance. Not used for fixed-geometry detector responses. Number must be followed by units; valid units are: meters, m, cm, mm, km, feet, ft, ', in, inches, or ". You may also add multiple distances, such as '3ft 4in', or '3.6E-2 m 12 cm' which are equivalent to 40inches and 15.6cm respectively.
Copies the table, as currently shown, to the clipboard, to paste into a spreadsheet or document.

Adds a checkbox to each row of the table, so you can choose which rows get copied to the clipboard, or exported to CSV. Rows start out checked; un-check the ones you dont want in the output. When this is un-checked, all rows are copied/exported.
Error computing the fluxes - please report this.
Failed to copy to clipboard - maybe a permissions issue - sorry.
Copied table to clipboard as HTML text.
Unknown result of copy command - sorry.
Uncertainties are statistical only; the detector efficiency does not have an uncertainty.
Uncertainties include the detector response's stated efficiency uncertainty ({1}%).
Uncertainties include {1}% efficiency uncertainty from the detector's geometry model only; the detector response states none of its own.
